details:
I think an interesting feature would be the ability for groups to have a "trust rank" much like players do.

Hypothetically, players of a certain trust rank would be able to give a thumbs up or thumbs down to any group whose instances they have joined in the past (or alternatively, players with higher trust ranks have exponentially more influence on the rating than lower trust ranks)

Poorly ranked groups would be deprioritized in the list of Group Public instances for any given world.

Exceptionally poorly ranked groups would have their Group Public instances shuffled off to a separate "bad group" list that people would have to opt in to see.

Well ranked groups would have their Group Public instances prioritized in the listings.

This would give an incentive for groups to take hosting their open instances seriously. Groups with troublemakers, absent mods, or "power-tripping moderators" would probably get downvoted and gradually see their ratings fall. While the well managed groups would continue to grow in size. 

This would also help with the problem of newer players joining the former type of group and being turned off the game due to bad first impressions.

There is a concern that "offsite brigading" could happen ("guys everone thumbs down this group because of x"), but this is combatted by:

- The player trust rank requirement (can't mass downvote using burner accounts)

- The "must have joined a hosted instance" requirement (can't get external followers involved)
title: Group Trust Ranks
